graph.title: Sky’s the Limit Convex Operating System Execution Graph
graph.objective: Maximize qualified visitor-to-signed-agreement-and-paid-deposit conversion while safely replacing fragmented Supabase, Payload, and Directus responsibilities with a Convex-centered operating system.
graph.sourceRequest: Turn this into a very efficient Loop and execution graph. Use this uploaded graph-engineer-codex-windows-v2 package as the canonical graph-engineering skill.

controlPattern.rationale: The program combines strict dependency gates, conflict-free workstreams, production/data/payment side effects, independent verification, bounded remediation loops, and reversible migration requirements.
controlPattern.synchronization: A node starts only after every dependsOn node succeeds, resource locks are free, risk authorization is recorded, and a Graphifyy-bounded node packet is generated from the current code graph.
controlPattern.termination: All required terminal gates through G90-DECOMMISSIONED succeed with evidence, no blocking risk remains, actual cost is recorded, and independent completion verification is produced.
controlPattern.recovery: replan from checkpoint; use retry-with-backoff for transient idempotent nodes and compensation chains for completed external side effects

assumptions: The audited repository and Vercel project remain the canonical implementation target.
Graphifyy is available or can be installed and refreshed incrementally.
Provider and owner-account access will be supplied at gated nodes.
ChatGPT Pro included agentic usage is consumed before purchased credits.
constraints: No destructive migration before snapshots, reconciliation, rollback evidence, and explicit approval.
No production payment, communication, GBP publication, cutover, or decommissioning without node-specific authorization.
Maximum concurrent agents is 8; economy mode defaults to one writer and at most one read-only worker.
Implementation agents receive bounded Graphifyy packets, not the full audit/wiki/graph report.
Authentication provider decision must be canonicalized before implementation and may not remain contradictory.

budgets.downgradePolicy: At 70%, stop new high-cost fan-out, route routine work to the cheapest capable model, compact context, and replan. At 95%, stop execution except rollback or evidence preservation.

risks.description: Incorrect identity or authorization migration could expose customer, property, project, or administrative data.
risks.mitigation: Block protected-surface expansion until independent authorization-matrix tests and approval gate pass.
risks.residualRisk: Provider misconfiguration or an untested resource type may remain.

risks.description: Supabase, Payload, Directus, and file migrations may omit, duplicate, or corrupt business records.
risks.mitigation: Immutable snapshots, legacy mappings, checksums, shadow reads, dual writes, reconciliation, and rollback drill.
risks.residualRisk: Unknown out-of-band production objects may be discovered late.

risks.description: Lead, estimate, proposal, signature, or deposit failures could lose revenue or acknowledge work that was not persisted.
risks.mitigation: Fail-closed persistence, idempotency, provider receipts, durable workflows, and conversion E2E gates.
risks.residualRisk: Third-party provider outages may delay processing.

risks.description: Route, canonical, content, or GBP errors could reduce local visibility or violate platform policy.
risks.mitigation: One route registry, crawl validation, policy-compliant review flow, human approval for GBP publishing.
risks.residualRisk: Search-engine recrawl timing is outside project control.

risks.description: Context duplication, agent fan-out, and failed retries could consume weekly agentic allowance inefficiently.
risks.mitigation: Graphifyy-bounded context packets, model routing, two-writer maximum, output schema, telemetry, and replan at 50% cost deviation.
risks.residualRisk: Complex debugging may require higher-cost model escalation.

risks.description: Production cutover or decommissioning could create downtime or destroy the rollback path.
risks.mitigation: Separate authorization, one active cutover node, tested rollback, observation window, and delayed decommissioning.
risks.residualRisk: External DNS/provider propagation can extend recovery time.

replanTriggers: actual cost deviates from expected by more than 50%
Graphifyy graph is stale or mis-bound
